os-3-30.alt: The cell cycle drawn as a circle. Most of the circle is interphase, split into G1, S and G2. A smaller wedge, labeled M, is the mitotic phase. Arrows lead from G1 out to G0, labeled as cells not actively dividing, and back.

os-3-32.alt: A row of drawings, each with a short list of events underneath and a fluorescence micrograph below, showing a cell passing through the stages of mitosis and then cytokinesis: chromosomes condense, line up across the middle, separate to opposite ends, and two new nuclei form as the cell pinches in two.

os-3-33.alt: The cell cycle circle with its checkpoints marked: one late in G1, one at the end of G2, and one during mitosis. Around the circle, four cyclin and cyclin-dependent kinase pairs are placed where each acts: two in G1, one in S and one at the step from G2 into mitosis.

os-3-36.alt: A branching chart of stem cells. At the top a totipotent cell gives rise to pluripotent cells, which give rise to multipotent cells, each of which produces a few related kinds of specialized cell.
